# CapSolver agent workflow

Use the core MCP for documentation and solver tasks; use the browser MCP for
page state and parameter acquisition. The browser process has no solver key and
cannot submit paid tasks. Tool availability is defined by tools/list. An external
browser MCP can substitute if it preserves the required state and evidence.

When tools/list includes capsolver_browser_attach, use browser_start to start
Chromium, then attach the active tab before its first navigation. For the
CapSolver workflow tools below use the capsolver_ prefix and the returned page
and session IDs. Native Patchright tools operate on the same selected tab.

## Establish the requested outcome

Use the user's target, permitted interaction and existing authorization. Identify
whether the goal is an API result, website acceptance, or reusable integration.
Ask only for missing conditions that block that goal: a permitted test page,
login access, triggering steps, proxy configuration, or a backend verification
endpoint. Do independent local work while waiting. Do not invent unavailable
inputs or treat documentation placeholders as valid live challenges.

Keep credentials in the existing environment or local secret files. Keep any
caller-supplied proxy credentials out of browser recipes and evidence. Follow the
user's storage and publication instructions.

## Determine the task contract

Call list_task_types, get_task_schema and get_docs for the actual type/variant.
Use get_supported_tasks, get_task_parameters or refresh_task_catalog to check
current official task documentation and differences. For DataDome, use
get_actual_user_agent with the actual platform, browser and major.
The catalog is a versioned snapshot, not a live OpenAPI source. Read current
official documentation when fields differ. Only explicitly choose
validation=provider after establishing the documented contract; never silently
change task types, proxy variants or validation mode to get a response.

Record required fields, their source, session/IP/UA constraints, expiry, the
complete solution shape, and the intended application/verification method.
An API key identifies the account; it does not make a non-Enterprise test site
an Enterprise site or make an unsupported sitekey supported.

## Acquire the current page's parameters

For dynamic pages read the acquisition guide, also available
as get_docs(topic="agent-acquisition"). Choose the least invasive source:

- DOM, a page global or the correct frame using browser_evaluate;
- a page-scoped init script installed before navigation;
- original response evidence captured before the initial request;
- a documented, newly issued context request when fresh registration is valid.

For early capture, open about:blank, add the init script, configure capture, then
navigate using browser_action. Alternatively supply response_capture in
browser_open to capture its first navigation. Already-loaded or missed traffic
cannot be recovered retroactively. A new request may consume or replace a
challenge; distinguish source=original_response from source=session_request.

Keep the same applicable exit, UA and session through acquisition, solve and
application. Attach to a browser the caller has configured when page traffic
needs a particular exit. browser_api_request uses context cookies and UA. For a
CDP attachment, allow_direct=true explicitly selects a separate direct request
with cookie synchronization. Use page operations and response capture when the
request needs to use the external browser's networking.

Use narrow capture globs. Raw URLs, headers, request bodies and response bytes
may contain credentials. Retain private local paths; expose only required fields
to the agent. Preserve large opaque data file-to-file instead of retyping it.
Never use truncated, pending, evicted or unavailable bodies as complete inputs.

## Prepare, submit and recover

Call browser_prepare_captcha with the fresh fields and recipe. This validates
the recipe and creates a captcha_id, task and optional task_file without charge.
Retain the session_id, page_id, captcha_id and capture response IDs. When the
selected task requires a proxy, add the caller's explicit proxy fields to the
solver task according to its schema. Keep ProxyLess tasks free of caller proxy
fields and keep acquisition configuration out of the solver task.

Submit via core create_task using one stable request_id for the logical request.
Use task OR task_file; both processes must share the file path for task_file.
If state=ready, use the whole solution; if processing, query/wait on its task_id.
After response loss use get_request_status with the same request_id. Local
deduplication requires the same persistent state directory/account/operator.

Read the recovery guide, also get_docs(topic="agent-recovery"),
for unknown submission, timeouts and official controls. Never create a new paid
task just because waiting ended. Do not replay a state-changing acquisition
request after a timeout without resolving whether the first was received.

## Apply and prove the outcome

For any task type, if the CapSolver response includes `solution.userAgent`,
use that exact User-Agent when applying or submitting the token. If the current
session cannot use it, report the mismatch and leave the page untouched.
For a known task ID, `get_actual_user_agent(task_id=...)` can read the returned
User-Agent. If the response omits it, follow the task's documented requirements.

Pass the full solution to browser_apply_solution in the prepared page. Respect
expiry, changed challenge fingerprints and already-used checks; do not disable
them. If a prepared challenge is stale, reacquire and prepare it again. A new
challenge can require a new authorized paid task; do not automatically reuse a
solution bound to the old one.

Submit only within the user's requested scope. Separate these outcomes:

1. Provider ready: solution-shaped API result.
2. Applied: callback/cookie/form changes executed.
3. Website accepted: explicit backend success or configured business condition.

HTTP 200, a populated hidden input or the disappearance of a widget alone is
not proof of backend acceptance. Report unavailable server verification as
unverified. Preserve checks for V3 score, action and hostname where relevant.
For reCAPTCHA, inspect error-codes even when success=true. Google's SiteVerify
can fail open above the site's quota with success=true and a fixed score of
0.9. Mark that assessment inconclusive and retain the warning. A site's billing
administrator must resolve its quota, or use a verifier with working quota.
Missing scores and verifier HTTP 500 responses remain unverified. Record
screenshot failures separately from completed backend checks, and retain the
leaf exceptions inside ExceptionGroup when diagnosing the capture step.

## Evidence and reusable delivery

Associate one run ID with the page/trigger, input source and timestamps, init
script, original response IDs/private files, prepared task, request_id/task_id,
solver HTTP evidence when available, full solution stored privately, application
steps and actual business response. Separate sanitized reports from private raw
files. The new acquisition tools do not automatically record raw solver HTTP;
use the existing audit harness when that evidence is required.

Report missing inputs, local failures and provider failures separately. If the
user requested MCP-first/official-second diagnosis, run a direct official
control after a failure only when budget and a valid fixture are available.
After both fail under comparable conditions, defer and retain evidence; do not
claim the precise upstream cause is known from a shared failure alone.

When requested, extract the verified workflow into a runnable integration with
configuration placeholders, a documented parameter source, bounded waiting,
recovery and the same success check. Do not present a local simulated fixture
as real provider or target-site acceptance.
agent-acquisition:
# Dynamic parameter acquisition

These examples describe the included 15-tool browser MCP. Actual tool names
must be obtained from tools/list. None of the four acquisition tools calls a
solver. Fetching page resources or registration endpoints is real network work
unless restricted to the owned loopback fixture.

## Capture before the first navigation

Open about:blank and keep the returned session_id/page_id. Register a JS
statement script using browser_add_init_script. The script runs on future page
navigations and child-frame documents, before page scripts. It does not run
retroactively. No explicit world flag is needed with this Playwright backend.
Order between independent init scripts is unspecified; use idempotent wrappers.
The source is retained locally with a script_id and SHA-256. At most 20 scripts
can be registered per page; open a new page/session to replace an installed set.

For an owned page that calls /challenge:

```javascript
(() => {
  if (window.__challengeCaptureInstalled) return;
  window.__challengeCaptureInstalled = true;
  window.__observedChallenges = [];
  const original = window.fetch;
  window.fetch = async function(...args) {
    const response = await original.apply(this, args);
    if (new URL(response.url).pathname === '/challenge') {
      response.clone().json().then(value => {
        window.__observedChallenges.push({value, receivedAt: Date.now()});
      }).catch(() => {});
    }
    return response;
  };
})();
```

This example only wraps fetch; XHR, WebSocket, workers or vendor render APIs
require an appropriate script or original-response capture. Do not assume a
fetch wrapper covers all browser traffic or arbitrary providers.

Configure browser_capture_responses with url_patterns such as
`["https://your-test-host.example/challenge*"]`, then navigate using
browser_action(action="navigate", options={"url": "..."}). For initial body
capture without a custom script, pass the same configuration as response_capture
to browser_open. Narrow globs operate against the full URL including its query.

Read browser_network_requests to obtain response_id and capture_state. Call
browser_get_response with include_body=false for file paths, or explicitly use
include_body=true to read selected bytes. Pagination offset/limit are byte-based;
use encoding=base64 for exact binary bytes or text to inspect UTF-8 JSON/HTML.
Parsing bytes locally avoids exposing opaque tokens to the model.

## Body representation, limits and lifecycle

Capture is opt-in. It saves the body returned by Playwright for the actual
response; content decompression may already have occurred. It is not a packet
trace and does not preserve compressed wire bytes, HTTP chunk framing or header
order. HTTP responses such as 403/500 are retained normally.

Defaults: 1 MB per body, 20 retained bodies per page. Maximum: 2 MB per body,
50 retained bodies, 16 MB total retained body bytes per page, and 100 metadata
records. In-flight original body jobs are also bounded. Older captured files
are deleted when evicted. Active record states can be pending, saved, truncated,
disabled, skipped_busy, skipped_stream, unavailable, cancelled or evicted.
Disabling capture stops new collection without deleting existing files.

The 15-second body timeout and streaming exclusions prevent indefinite waits.
Retention limits do not bound Playwright's internal network buffers. If full
inputs exceed the configured limit, use a separately authorized acquisition
method instead of passing the retained prefix as a complete challenge.

Evidence lives beneath CAPSOLVER_STATE_DIR/browser-evidence in random per-session,
per-page directories. Leaf directories are 0700 and files 0600. Raw metadata can
contain full URLs, headers/Cookies and request bodies. Tool summaries omit query
values and raw headers. Body inclusion is explicit for original-response reads.
Files remain after browser_close for investigation, subject to per-page eviction;
there is no global disk quota. Remove the run directory when its retention period
ends. Do not commit or upload it. Shared-file deployment is needed to inspect
files from a different process or host.

## Make a documented new request

browser_api_request accepts url, method, optional headers/data, timeout_ms,
follow_redirects, max_body_bytes, include_body and allow_direct. Managed sessions
use context.request. A separate request for a CDP attachment requires
allow_direct=true and synchronizes changed cookies back to the page. Use the
external page's own operations and capture for traffic through its configured
network. Avoid concurrent page traffic changing
the same cookies during synchronization. It saves evidence with
source=session_request and is_new_request=true. It does not navigate the page.

GET is the default. POST and other state changes must fit the user's existing
authorization. There are no automatic network retries. The CapSolver API host
is blocked by this tool; use core tools to preserve task accounting and recovery.
This does not restrict privileged page scripts or external HTTP programs.
Redirect following is off by default. When enabled, at most five redirects are followed, offline
destination rules apply on every hop, and explicit authorization/cookie headers
are removed on cross-origin hops. Stored metadata identifies explicit headers;
it does not claim to enumerate automatically attached Cookie/UA transport headers.

An HTTP failure is a completed request with http_ok=false, not proof of a tool
failure. A timeout/transport failure can mean delivery_unknown: use its local
metadata evidence and do not assume the server received nothing. Original body
reads never issue this tool's new requests implicitly.

## Preserve task validity

Match the page's origin, effective UA and applicable proxy to the task contract.
Cookies alone do not guarantee IP/session/fingerprint equivalence. A registration
request can rotate a challenge. Do not combine an old page's challenge with a
new registration response unless documented. Reacquire from one coherent flow.

Pass selected fields through task_overrides or a recipe to
browser_prepare_captcha. Inspect the prepared task before creating a paid task.
The capture configuration, response IDs, evidence paths and script IDs are local
provenance, not provider task fields.

## DataDome challenge and replay checks

Before submitting a paid task, check the actual challenge page, not only its URL.
For a slider, require a current /captcha/ URL with t=fe and a visible interactive
slider; t=bv or a restriction page is not a solvable slider. Interstitials use
/interstitial/ and must be identified separately; do not infer that they are
blocked merely because they lack the slider's t parameter.

Preparation now requires captchaUrl to match exactly one loaded challenge frame.
The workflow binds that frame and document; navigation, replacement or reload
invalidates the prepared result and returns STALE_CHALLENGE before application.
Keep the existing provider task/result for recovery; do not automatically submit
a replacement. A new challenge requires fresh preparation and an authorized round.

Keep the selected sticky proxy, effective browser User-Agent and challenge
session consistent. If authorized to change proxy, establish a new sticky
session and reacquire the challenge; do not reuse a URL from the previous exit.
Independent exit checks and any IP displayed by the challenge can detect some
mismatches, but cannot prove the solver worker's actual exit. When needed,
include the HTML from the current challenge frame, not unrelated top-page HTML.

Apply the complete returned Cookie to the attached tab's own browser context.
Confirm that the real follow-up request sends that Cookie and that the target
backend accepts it. Cookie parsing and target scope are checked before mutation;
a successful write must also be readable in the target context. For local
acceptance runs, take a navigation_checkpoint immediately before application,
then pass it to protected_validation.snapshot(after=...). Cookie and status must
come from the same new response, with no document change during inspection. The workflow's target-scoped CDP cookie write must be retained;
a default-context cookie write is incorrect for isolated contexts. A 403 response
or a non-JSON body must not be treated as a successful JSON verification.

If the follow-up page presents another genuinely new, visible solvable challenge,
use fresh parameters in the same session only within an explicitly authorized
round budget. The local acceptance recipe uses at most two rounds. Stop on a
restriction page or an unknown submission result instead of repeating a paid task.

For an interstitial-to-slider transition, retain the current browser context,
network exit, effective UA and Cookie jar. A ready interstitial result followed
by a fresh visible slider is an unfinished challenge sequence. Prepare the new
slider using its current captchaUrl and, when supplied, its actual frame HTML;
use a new captcha_id and request_id for that new challenge. Do not reuse the
interstitial URL or launch another browser between these two rounds. Keep each
round's API result, Cookie transmission and website verdict separate.

Wait for the iframe document and its response, not only the iframe element's
attachment. Recheck the active challenge immediately before submission. Some
slider templates retain a blocked-looking document title while the rendered
body displays a usable t=fe slider; classify using the current URL and visible
body together. A t=bv URL or an actual restriction body still stops the flow.
If a failed round leaves no fresh matching challenge for an official control,
record the control as not submitted. A new proxy/session control changes the
comparison conditions and must be labeled separately.
agent-recovery:
# Failure classification and recovery

| Observation | Action | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing required fields or wrong variant | Read the actual schema/docs; acquire the missing fields before submission | Submitting placeholder values |
| Initial dynamic request already occurred | Install capture before a permitted new page flow, or use a documented fresh registration endpoint | Claiming a new request is the original response |
| Original response pending | Read its response_id again; inspect bounded capture state | Re-fetching implicitly |
| Body truncated, unavailable or evicted | Report missing complete evidence; reacquire only within scope | Passing partial HTML/images as full input |
| Context request timeout | Inspect delivery_unknown evidence; check target state if possible | Replaying a potentially received POST automatically |
| Provider processing | Continue querying the same task_id within its expiry/budget | Creating a second task |
| Local wait timeout | Preserve task_id and resume later | Calling the task failed or cancelled |
| Lost create response | get_request_status with the original request_id and persistent store | New request_id or clearing the store |
| Ready metadata but RESULT_NOT_CACHED after restart | For an asynchronous task, query get_task_result with its original task_id within its age/query limits | Creating a replacement task or assuming the stored metadata contains the solution |
| acceptance_unknown without recoverable task_id | Report unresolved provider acceptance; use provider/account evidence or support | Assuming no charge/submission occurred |
| Same request_id with changed fields | Resolve the original logical request; use a deliberately new ID only for an authorized new attempt | Bypassing the fingerprint conflict silently |
| Expired or changed prepared challenge | Reacquire and prepare again, preserving original evidence | Disabling freshness/consumed checks |
| Provider ready but page rejects | Check full solution, callback, Cookie scope, UA/proxy, freshness and backend response | Counting token presence as success |
| Official API rejects a sitekey/type | Check task/site variant and supported test inputs | Treating account tier as the cause without evidence |

## Direct official API controls

When the user requests MCP-first/official-second comparison, preserve the failed
MCP request first. A direct official control needs equivalent valid inputs and
the same applicable proxy, UA and page state. Do not reuse consumed one-time
parameters. If fresh inputs are required, record that the runs differ.

Create at most the authorized additional task budget. Save the actual submitted
task, sanitized HTTP request/response evidence, task_id and website application.
Use the existing local audit/control harness; these browser tools alone do not
capture solver transport. Stop on definitive unsupported input or insufficient
credit rather than cycling through unrelated sites or task types.

If both fail, classify as an upstream/input/fixture issue pending investigation;
this is not proof of the provider's precise internal root cause. If direct API
succeeds while MCP fails under comparable conditions, inspect our conversion,
task validation, HTTP serialization, complete solution preservation and application.

## Report each layer separately

- Missing test conditions: identify the precise missing page, supported key,
  fresh challenge, proxy or backend verification capability.
- Local defect: include the failing stage, reproducible arguments and local
  evidence; keep original secrets private.
- Upstream error: retain exact sanitized error code/subcode and HTTP status,
  distinguishing an explicit provider failure from a transport uncertainty.
- Incomplete verification: an API result or page injection is not a failed
  business verification unless the target actually rejected it.

Retry only when there is a reason the next attempt differs or an explicitly
authorized bounded retry policy applies. Waiting, unknown acceptance and
terminal provider failure are different states. Never import an unlimited
"repeat until solved" rule from a competitor's agent instructions.

The synchronous get_token provider exchange has a separate 120-second default
budget (CAPSOLVER_GET_TOKEN_TIMEOUT, up to 120 seconds). Keep the MCP client's
own call budget above it. The submission deadline is stored with the request;
status reads and other workers must honor it. A timeout without a task ID stays
acceptance_unknown and must not be automatically submitted again.
